title: VP’s ex-staff never held captive – lawyer
summary: A lawyer representing the businessman who employed Vice President Sara Duterte’s former household staff maintained that they were neither held captive nor forced to sign affidavits intended to…

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte visits quake victims in Davao Occidental, as seen in photos posted June 26, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — A lawyer representing the businessman who employed Vice President Sara Duterte’s former household staff maintained that they were neither held captive nor forced to sign affidavits intended to malign Duterte.

“My client categorically denies the allegation that two former employees of Vice President Sara Duterte were held captive. He states that both women remained reachable throughout the period in question and that he continues to communicate with them regularly,” said Mark Tolentino.

In his social media account, Tolentino spoke on behalf of his client, the businessman mentioned in the incident involving Duterte’s former staff, who sought the help of the Vice President on Monday and reportedly claimed being threatened.
With the help of the police and Duterte’s legal team, they have been released from their employers’ care.
They were brought to a police station to execute affidavits on the incident.

Tolentino said his client has no affiliation with any government or law enforcement agency under the Marcos administration and only approached government authorities in his capacity as a private citizen and employer to seek security assistance for his employees, himself and his family.

Paolo Panelo, Duterte’s spokesperson, claimed the employer told the former household helpers that the threats against them would be quelled if they executed affidavits, drafts of which were presented to them.
Panelo said the Vice President is conducting an internal investigation into the circumstances surrounding the case.

“Regardless, it is noteworthy that despite the claim that the affidavits were meant to secure protection, the effect seemed to be the opposite. The house staffers felt so unsafe that they immediately sought the assistance of the Vice President for safe passage,” he said.
The businessman has not been publicly identified.
